downside.story: 10th percentile ($107.6): AI capex digestion toward the standing file low case (customer capex -20% vs base in every forecast quarter: CY27 ~$1.47T, CY28 ~$1.80T), Marvell share of wallet -10% (custom ramps slip a year, an AWS Trainium generation goes elsewhere), gross margin -1.5pt on custom mix and price; FY28 revenue $14.7B and FY29 $20.9B (vs $19.6B / $28.2B base); P/E -9 turns (20.0x NTM, the 2022-23 de-rating level). Deal: signed and pending, with module makers moving DSP orders (the dis-synergy side), held at the expected-value weight. The pct deltas also hit Q3-Q4 FY27 mechanically (FY27 $10.3B), harsher than the guided Q3 but small for the horizon value.

upside.story: 90th percentile ($381.8): customer capex 12% above base (between base and the file high case), share of wallet +8% (custom >$12B FY29 as guided, Google TPU-attach programmes, scale-up optics from Celestial), gross margin +0.5pt; FY28 $23.3B (above the ~$20B target) and FY29 $33.7B (consensus $31.3B); P/E +5 turns (34.0x). downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex 22% below the base path (toward the file low case: 2027 ~$1,390B, 2028 ~$1,265B) as lab/neocloud financing tightens; Marvell loses custom share (Trainium 3/4 at Alchip, an XPU programme slips) and LPO/CPO trims DSP content: share -10%; GM -1.5pt on deleverage; P/E -9 turns (~25x after SBC). Deal: signed at a richer premium with the Stifel-sized or larger DSP-customer backlash (V nearer -$10B than -$2.4B); the engine keeps the expected-value adjustment, the case's multiple carries the rest.

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex tracks the file's high path (2027 ~$2.2-2.4T) and Marvell hits the investor-day FY28 ~$20B and FY29 custom >$12B with scale-up optics ramping (share +7%); GM +0.5pt; P/E +6 turns. Deal: either walked away from (no dilution) or closed near market with laser-supply and CPO synergies and no material customer loss (V around +$5B).

downside.story: 10th percentile (~$98): hyperscalers digest in CY2027-28 (AI capex 25% below the standing base, near the file's low case), Marvell content per capex dollar 8% lower (Trainium generation to Alchip, Microsoft dual-sources), custom mix takes GM 2pt lower, and the market pays ~18.8x for decelerating EPS; the Lumentum deal is signed at an ~8% premium and module makers move DSP orders (the dis-synergy sits at its high end).

downside.story: P10: an AI capex digestion starts in 2027 (standing file low case: 2027 $1,390B vs base $1,841B, 2028 $1,265B): customer capex -22% and Marvell's share of wallet -10% in every forecast quarter (custom programs slip, Trainium share to Alchip, Microsoft late), so DC revenue ~30% below base; C&O -10%; GM -2pt on under-absorption, opex only -4%; the market re-rates AI semis to ~21x NTM. upside.story: P90: toward the standing file high case (customer capex +15%) with Google TPU-attach programs and scale-up optics landing early (share of wallet +6%): FY28 revenue ~$23B (above the $20B target, in line with Marvell's habit of raising targets every quarter in 2026), FY29 ~$34B; GM holds ~57.4%; the multiple re-rates to ~35x on visibility from the Google warrant tranches; Lumentum either priced near market with laser-supply synergies and no customer backlash, or abandoned.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex follows the file's low path (CY27 1,390 / CY28 1,265, a 2028 digestion year), Marvell loses share on one hyperscaler XPU generation and the Google ramp slips (dc_share -12%), margins fall 4 points on under-absorbed opex, the P/E de-rates 9 turns (~19x, NVDA/AVGO levels; the normalised leg to 16x), and the Lumentum deal closes at the reported terms (kept at expected value; at signing with DSP-customer backlash the case is a few dollars lower).

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex digestion toward the standing file low case (customer capex -20% vs base every forecast quarter), Marvell share of wallet -10% (custom ramps slip a year; optical-DSP share lost to Broadcom/Credo if module makers react to a Marvell-Lumentum combination), gross margin -1.5pt; P/E -9 turns (18.5x, the 2022-23 de-rating level).
